polish_source_replacements.after: A binary relation \(\succeq\) on a set \(A\) is complete if \(a \succeq b\) or \(b \succeq a\) for every \(a \in A\) and \(b \in A\), reflexive if \(a \succeq a\) for every \(a \in A\), and transitive if \(a \succeq c\) whenever \(a \succeq b\) and \(b \succeq c\). A preference relation is a complete reflexive transitive binary relation. If \(a \succeq b\) but not \(b \succeq a\) then we write \(a \succ b\); if \(a \succeq b\) and \(b \succeq a\) then we write \(a \sim b\). A preference relation \(\succeq\) on \(A\) is continuous if \(a \succeq b\) whenever there are sequences \((a_k)_k\) and \((b_k)_k\) in \(A\) that converge to \(a\) and \(b\) respectively for which \(a_k \succeq b_k\) for all \(k\). A preference relation \(\succeq\) on \(\mathbb { R } ^ n\) is quasi-concave if for every \(b \in \mathbb { R } ^ n\) the set \(\{a \in \mathbb { R } ^ n : a \succeq b\}\) is convex; it is strictly quasi-concave if every such set is strictly convex.
